intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Walk across Sultanahmet Square to the stunning Blue Mosque, admiring its six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide to uncover the layered Byzantine and Ottoman history embedded in every stone.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Market Food and Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and aromatic spices. Engage with local vendors, bargain for handcrafted ceramics and textiles, and taste free samples of regional delicacies along the way.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the sprawling Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Harem, the Treasury housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, and the sacred relics pavilion. The palace gardens offer breathtaking panoramic views over the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn, and the Sea of Marmara.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Mezes
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden gulet for a scenic sunset cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, the waterway dividing Europe and Asia. Sail past Ottoman-era yalı mansions, the Rumeli Fortress, and the iconic suspension bridges. Enjoy a spread of authentic Turkish mezes — stuffed grape leaves, hummus, grilled halloumi, and fresh seafood — paired with local Efes beer or çay (tea).

experiences.name: Balık Ekmek & Street Food Walk in Karaköy
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided street food journey through the vibrant Karaköy neighborhood. Start with a classic balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the floating boats near Galata Bridge, then explore simit carts, börek bakeries, and roasted chestnut vendors. End the evening at a traditional meyhane (tavern) in nearby Beyoğlu for a full rakı and meze dinner experience with live fasıl music.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Havaist airport bus (approx. 100 TL) to Sultanahmet. Check into your boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia from the plaza — free of charge.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Hippodrome of Constantinople (At Meydanı), see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column for free. Enjoy the atmospheric evening light over the historic peninsula.

meals.breakfast: On the plane.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick simit (sesame bread ring) and ayran from a street cart near the airport bus stop — under 50 TL total.
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi (famous local köfte restaurant on Divan Yolu) — a classic, affordable bowl of lentil soup and köfte plate for around 150–200 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Get an Istanbulkart (transit card) at the airport or a nearby kiosk — it saves money on all public transport. Exchange a small amount of cash at a bank or ATM (avoid airport exchange counters for best rates).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (free entry as a mosque — dress modestly, bring a scarf). Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at the Byzantine mosaics and Ottoman calligraphy. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Topkapi Palace (entry fee approx. 500–700 TL — one of the best value historic sites in the city). Walk through the Imperial Gate, the Harem courtyards, and the Treasury. The views over the Bosphorus from the palace gardens are stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to Eminönü waterfront. Watch the ferries and fishermen on the Galata Bridge. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of the Golden Horn at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel (if included) or a local bakery — börek (cheese or spinach pastry) and tea for 50–80 TL.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Topkapi Palace cafeteria or pack a simit and fruit from a street vendor to eat in the palace gardens.
meals.dinner: Balıkçı stalls on the Galata Bridge — freshly grilled fish sandwich (balık ekmek) for around 80–100 TL each. Eat standing at the water's edge like a true local.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — Sunday is a great day to visit. The Harem is a separate ticket (worth it). Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — completely free. Admire the 20,000 Iznik tiles and six minarets. Walk next door to the Arasta Bazaar, a quieter alternative to the Grand Bazaar with less pressure to buy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — free to enter. One of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with 4,000+ shops. Browse leather goods, ceramics, spices, and textiles. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) near Eminönü — free entry. Sample spices, Turkish delight, and dried fruits. Pick up affordable local snacks for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a local kahvaltı café near Sultanahmet — olives, cheese, tomatoes, eggs, bread, and çay (tea) for 100–150 TL.
meals.lunch: Eat at a lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) inside or near the Grand Bazaar — a full plate of stew, rice, and salad for 120–180 TL.
meals.dinner: Lezzet-i Şark or similar neighborhood restaurant near Sultanahmet — pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) or lahmacun for 80–130 TL.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays — Monday is perfect. Carry small bills for bargaining. Don't feel obligated to buy; browsing is perfectly normal.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex (entry approx. 300–400 TL) — three museums in one: the main archaeology museum with the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk Museum. Truly world-class collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Gülhane Park (free) — Istanbul's oldest public park, adjacent to Topkapi. Stroll among rose gardens and enjoy panoramic Bosphorus views. Visit the small Museum of the History of Science and Technology in Islam inside the park (low entry fee).
day_by_day.evening: Take a tram (Istanbulkart) up Divan Yolu, the ancient Roman road that once connected the city. Stop at the Column of Constantine (Çemberlitaş) — a free outdoor monument over 1,600 years old.

meals.breakfast: Simit from a street cart and a glass of fresh-squeezed pomegranate or orange juice from a juice stand — 40–60 TL.
meals.lunch: Canteen-style lunch at a lokanta near Gülhane — soup, main, and bread for under 150 TL.
meals.dinner: Şehzade Cağ Kebabı near Sultanahmet — try the famous cağ kebab (Erzurum-style spit-roasted lamb) for around 150–200 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Note: Topkapi Palace is closed today (Tuesday), but the Archaeological Museums are open. Plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Take the tram to Karaköy and walk up the steep hill (or take the historic Tünel funicular — one of the world's oldest, just a couple of TL) to Beyoğlu. Explore the bohemian Galata neighborhood and climb the Galata Tower (entry approx. 350–500 TL) for panoramic 360° views of Istanbul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down famous İstiklal Avenue (Istiklal Caddesi) — a 1.4km pedestrian boulevard with historic buildings, bookshops, music stores, and street performers. Free to explore. Duck into side streets to find local cafés, vintage shops, and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Karaköy's trendy café and street food scene. Visit the waterfront area and watch the Bosphorus ferries at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a Sultanahmet bakery before heading out.
meals.lunch: Karaköy Güllüoğlu — famous baklava shop in Karaköy. Have a generous portion of baklava with tea as a light lunch treat for 80–120 TL.
meals.dinner: Meyhane (traditional tavern) in Beyoğlu — order a selection of cold mezze (hummus, haydari, dolma, cacık) and share. Budget around 200–250 TL per person.

day_by_day.notes: May 19 is a national holiday in Turkey (Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day) — expect festive atmosphere, possible street events, and some sites may have altered hours.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to the Asian side — Kadıköy district. The regular commuter ferry (Istanbulkart) costs only 20–30 TL and offers spectacular views of the skyline, mosques, and palaces. Far better value than tourist cruise boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kadıköy's vibrant market district (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a foodie paradise with fresh produce, cheese shops, fishmongers, and delis. Browse Moda neighborhood's charming streets and waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Eminönü as the sun sets over the European skyline — one of Istanbul's most magical free experiences.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure at your hotel or grab a simit on the way to the ferry.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Kadıköy market — fresh fish, köfte, or börek from market stalls for 100–150 TL total.
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — legendary restaurant serving rare Anatolian regional dishes. A must for food lovers. Budget 200–300 TL for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Kadıköy ferry is a genuine local commuter service — use your Istanbulkart. Avoid overpriced tourist boat tours. Kadıköy has a very different, more secular and youthful vibe than the historic peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most beautiful imperial mosque, designed by the legendary architect Sinan. Free entry. The mosque sits on a hilltop with sweeping Golden Horn views. Explore the surrounding historic neighborhood of Süleymaniye.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Fatih district — one of Istanbul's most traditional and authentic neighborhoods. Visit the Fatih Mosque (free) and explore the local street market if it's running. This area offers a genuine window into conservative Ottoman-era Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via tram. Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — a dramatic underground Byzantine water cistern with atmospheric lighting (entry approx. 300–400 TL). Book ahead if possible.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a local Sultanahmet café — 100–150 TL.
meals.lunch: Eat at a lokanta in the Süleymaniye area — frequented by locals and university students, very affordable. Full meal for 100–130 TL.
meals.dinner: Döner kebab from a reputable local shop near Sultanahmet — a generous portion with salad and bread for 100–150 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the Islamic holy day — the Süleymaniye Mosque will be busiest at midday prayer. Plan your visit for mid-morning. Remove shoes before entering any mosque.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar). Catch the ferry from Kabataş or Eminönü to Büyükada, the largest island (ferry approx. 80–120 TL round trip with Istanbulkart). No cars on the islands — only horse-drawn carriages and bicycles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle on Büyükada (approx. 100–150 TL for a few hours) and cycle around the island's pine forests and Victorian-era mansions. Climb to the Monastery of Saint George (Aya Yorgi) for spectacular sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Take the late afternoon ferry back to Istanbul. Arrive in time for a relaxed evening dinner in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast or eat before departure — the ferry terminal has simit and tea sellers.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant on Büyükada waterfront — fresh fish, salad, and bread for 200–300 TL (slightly pricier on the island, but worth it for the setting).
meals.dinner: Simple pide or lahmacun at a neighborhood restaurant near your hotel — 100–150 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to the Princes' Islands are busy on weekends — arrive at the terminal 30 minutes early. The island is a perfect escape from the city bustle. Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — famous for its extraordinary Byzantine mosaics and frescoes (entry approx. 200–300 TL). Take the tram and a bus or walk from Sultanahmet (about 30–40 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls — the massive 5th-century land walls that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. Stretch for 6km across the city. Free to walk along and explore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a rooftop café or tea garden with views of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Börek and tea at a local pastane (pastry shop) near your hotel — 60–80 TL.
meals.lunch: Eat in the Edirnekapı/Fatih area — local lokanta with a view of the city walls. 100–150 TL.
meals.dinner: Tarihi Karadeniz Pide Salonu or similar pide restaurant in Sultanahmet — 120–180 TL for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church may have restricted access if undergoing restoration — check current status before visiting. The area around the walls is quiet and authentic — a very different Istanbul from the tourist center.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş (entry approx. 500–700 TL) — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore, where Atatürk spent his final days. Guided tours only; book the morning slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, working-class district with a famous street market (pazarı) on Mondays. Browse fresh produce, cheap clothing, and local goods. Soak up authentic Istanbul street life.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Bosphorus promenade from Beşiktaş toward Ortaköy. Visit the iconic Ortaköy Mosque at sunset — one of Istanbul's most photogenic spots, with the Bosphorus Bridge looming behind it.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery near Sultanahmet.
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market food stalls — fresh simit, roasted chestnuts, gözleme (stuffed flatbread), and fruit for under 100 TL.
meals.dinner: Ortaköy kumpir (stuffed baked potato) — a famous local street food specialty. A loaded kumpir with all toppings costs around 100–150 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe is a splurge but architecturally extraordinary. Photography inside is restricted. The Beşiktaş market is a wonderful authentic experience — bring cash.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern art museum in Karaköy (entry approx. 200–300 TL) — Turkey's leading contemporary art museum with rotating international exhibitions and a permanent collection of Turkish modern art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Galata and Karaköy waterfront area. Visit the historic Yeraltı Camii (Underground Mosque) — a unique mosque built in a Byzantine-era underground structure. Free entry. Walk through the atmospheric narrow streets of old Galata.
day_by_day.evening: Take the tram back to Sultanahmet and visit the Mosaic Museum (Great Palace Mosaics Museum) — houses stunning in-situ Byzantine floor mosaics from the 5th–6th century (entry approx. 150–250 TL). Often overlooked by tourists.

meals.breakfast: Simit and fresh juice from a Sultanahmet street cart — 50–70 TL.
meals.lunch: Karaköy street food — midye dolma (stuffed mussels sold from street carts) are a quintessential Istanbul experience. 5–10 TL per mussel.
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant near Eminönü — slightly above budget but famous for southeastern Turkish cuisine and spectacular Golden Horn views. Kebab meal around 250–350 TL. Alternatively, eat at a cheaper local kebab house for 150 TL.

day_by_day.notes: The Mosaic Museum is tucked behind the Arasta Bazaar near the Blue Mosque — easy to combine with an evening stroll. Midye dolma (stuffed mussels) should only be eaten from busy carts with high turnover for food safety.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) experience — visit Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Cağaloğlu Hamamı, both historic 16th–17th century bathhouses near Sultanahmet. A basic self-service entry is the most budget-friendly option (approx. 400–600 TL including towel and soap). A wonderful cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a final afternoon revisiting your favorite spots in Sultanahmet. Sit in the Sultanahmet square gardens, people-watch, sketch, journal, or simply absorb the atmosphere. Visit any museums or sites you missed.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the waterfront at Eminönü for a final sunset view. Cross the Galata Bridge on foot — look down at the fishermen and look back at the illuminated skyline of the historic peninsula. A perfect farewell to Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional Turkish breakfast at a proper kahvaltı spot — treat yourself on this second-to-last day. 150–200 TL.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a rooftop café in Sultanahmet with Blue Mosque views — çorba (soup) and bread for 80–120 TL.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — try İskender kebab (thinly sliced döner over bread with tomato sauce and butter) at a reputable spot. 200–300 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance online if possible — walk-in is fine but morning slots fill up. The hammam experience typically lasts 1.5–2 hours. Bring flip-flops.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. If your flight is late, take one last stroll through Sultanahmet. Visit the Arasta Bazaar for any last-minute souvenir shopping — ceramics, evil eye charms (nazar boncuğu), spices, and Turkish delight are good budget-friendly gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, head to the airport via Havaist bus from Sultanahmet/Taksim area (allow 1.5–2 hours for the journey including check-in time). Return your Istanbulkart or keep it as a souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Carry memories of one of the world's great cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café — olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumber, eggs, and endless çay.
meals.lunch: A last simit or börek from a street cart on the way to the bus stop — the perfect budget Istanbul farewell meal.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time to reach the airport — Istanbul traffic can be unpredictable. The Havaist bus is reliable and far cheaper than a taxi. Keep some TL for the bus fare. Check in online the night before if possible.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Sultanahmet boutique hotel (approx. 45–60 min by airport metro + tram or taxi). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation stroll around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia from the square without entering — perfect low-key introduction after a long flight. Walk along the Hippodrome (At Meydanı) and see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet. Head to Divan Yolu Caddesi for a relaxed first dinner. Enjoy a gentle evening walk back to the hotel along the illuminated historic landmarks.

meals.breakfast: On the plane / airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or upon arrival — try a simit (sesame bread ring) with cheese from a street cart near Sultanahmet for ~20–30 TRY
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — iconic, affordable köfte (meatball) restaurant on Divan Yolu; budget ~200–300 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Hydrate well, exchange some currency or use ATM near the hotel, and pick up a local SIM card at the airport for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) when it opens — arrive early (8:30–9:00) to beat crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring this UNESCO World Heritage marvel, once a Byzantine cathedral, then Ottoman mosque, now an active mosque open to visitors (dress modestly, cover head for women).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Topkapi Palace complex. Spend 3–4 hours exploring the palace courtyards, the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the Harem (separate ticket). Enjoy views over the Bosphorus from the palace terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to the Eminönü waterfront. Watch the ferries and fishermen on Galata Bridge. Browse the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) if still open (closes ~19:00). Enjoy dinner near the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a classic Turkish breakfast spread (menemen, olives, white cheese, tomatoes) at a local kahvaltı place for ~150–200 TRY
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds — mid-range, great views; ~300–400 TRY per person
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant near Eminönü — famous for kebabs with panoramic Bosphorus views; ~400–500 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace and Hagia Sophia tickets can be purchased online in advance to save queuing time. Hagia Sophia is free but closes during prayer times — check the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — free entry, open to non-worshippers between prayer times. Spend 45 minutes inside admiring the 20,000 İznik tiles and six minarets. Then visit the nearby Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) to see stunning 6th-century Byzantine floor mosaics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) — a world-class complex with the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Near Eastern artifacts, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. Easily 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for a relaxed evening. Walk through the Grand Bazaar area (closes ~19:00 on weekdays) for a peek at the labyrinthine covered market. Enjoy dinner in a rooftop restaurant with views of the illuminated domes and minarets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Casual pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at Tarihi Karadeniz Pide Salonu near the bazaar area; ~150–200 TRY
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant in Sultanahmet — Ottoman cuisine in a historic setting; ~450–600 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque is under ongoing restoration — some sections may be partially screened but still visitable. Check prayer times before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with 4,000+ shops. Explore the hans (merchant courtyards), jewelry section, ceramics, textiles, and antiques. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — Sinan's masterpiece, less crowded than the Blue Mosque, with sweeping Golden Horn views. Explore the surrounding neighborhood of Süleymaniye, a quieter, more residential historic quarter. Visit the tomb of Suleiman the Magnificent.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Beyazıt neighborhood and the old book bazaar (Sahaflar Çarşısı). Take the tram back to Sultanahmet for dinner. Optional: catch a traditional Turkish music performance at a local cultural center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) restaurants near Süleymaniye — try Darüzziyafe in the mosque's historic soup kitchen building; ~250–350 TRY
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin in Sultanahmet — beloved traditional fish restaurant; ~400–500 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Grand Bazaar — the cobblestones are uneven. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Golden Horn to explore Beyoğlu. Take the historic Galata Bridge on foot (15–20 min walk from Sultanahmet) or hop on the tram to Karaköy. Climb the 14th-century Galata Tower for panoramic 360° views of Istanbul — arrive early to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll up İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European-style buildings, boutiques, cafés, and street musicians. Explore the side streets (Asmalımescit, Cihangir) for local art galleries and independent shops. Visit the Pera Museum with its famous Orientalist paintings.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Beyoğlu for dinner and evening atmosphere. The neighborhood comes alive at night with restaurants, meyhanes (taverns), and live music.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a simit and Turkish tea (çay) from a street vendor near Karaköy
meals.lunch: Karaköy Güllüoğlu — legendary baklava shop in Karaköy; pair with a Turkish coffee for a sweet lunch break; then grab a lahmacun (Turkish flatbread) from a nearby spot; ~100–150 TRY
meals.dinner: Meyhane dinner at Refik in Asmalımescit — classic Istanbul tavern with meze and rakı; ~400–550 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Galata Tower ticket can be booked online. İstiklal Avenue is very busy on weekends — a Wednesday visit is more relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry cruise — board a public İDO/Şehir Hatları ferry from Eminönü for the full Bosphorus tour (approx. 90 min each way to Anadolu Kavağı). Enjoy views of Ottoman palaces, yalıs (waterfront mansions), fortresses, and the bridge connecting Europe and Asia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian side. Hike up to the ruins of Yoros Castle (Genoese Castle) for spectacular views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the small fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Eminönü in the late afternoon. Stop at Eminönü for a famous balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the boats moored at the dock — a quintessential Istanbul street food experience. Return to Sultanahmet for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start recommended)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at one of the simple fish restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — grilled fish, salad, and bread; ~300–400 TRY per person
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a neighborhood lokanta near the hotel — try mercimek çorbası (lentil soup), stuffed peppers, and ayran; ~150–200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is very affordable (~50–80 TRY round trip) and far more authentic than tourist boat tours. Check the İDO timetable the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii/Museum) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, recently restored. Take a taxi or bus (30–40 min from Sultanahmet). Also walk a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historically layered districts along the Golden Horn. Wander past the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, the Fener Greek Boys' School (Red Castle), and the rainbow-colored houses of Balat. Browse antique shops and local cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via taxi or bus. Relax at a traditional Turkish hammam — try Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584, designed by Sinan) for a classic bathing and scrub experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Balat at a local café — try a simple menemen (egg and tomato dish) or a homemade börek; ~150–200 TRY
meals.dinner: Sefa Restaurant near Sultanahmet — traditional Turkish home cooking; ~200–300 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The hammam experience at Çemberlitaş costs approximately 600–900 TRY for the full treatment. Book ahead or arrive early. Bring flip-flops and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy (25 min, very affordable). Explore the vibrant Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a lively food market with spices, cheeses, olives, fresh produce, and local delicacies. A paradise for food lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Moda neighborhood of Kadıköy — a charming, bohemian seaside district with tree-lined streets, independent bookshops, vintage stores, and lovely waterfront promenade. Enjoy the authentic, local (non-touristy) atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet by ferry. Optional: stop at Karaköy on the way back for a craft coffee and pastry. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Graze through Kadıköy Market — try kokoreç (offal sandwich), fresh döner, midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and seasonal fruit; budget ~100–150 TRY for a full market lunch
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant at Four Seasons Sultanahmet — a mid-range splurge in a converted Ottoman prison; ~600–800 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is very popular on Saturdays — arrive at the market by 10:00 for the best experience before crowds peak. The ferry ride itself is a highlight with great city views.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore, with 285 rooms, 44 halls, and a 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier. Guided tours only; book tickets in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Beşiktaş neighborhood. Visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) with its collection of imperial caïques (royal barges) and Ottoman maritime history. Then explore the lively Beşiktaş market area and waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Take a taxi or bus to the trendy Nişantaşı neighborhood for upscale window shopping and café culture. Or return to Sultanahmet for a quieter evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start for Dolmabahçe)
meals.lunch: Café Dolmabahçe inside the palace grounds or a nearby Beşiktaş restaurant — try a fresh fish sandwich by the waterfront; ~200–250 TRY
meals.dinner: Vogue Restaurant in Beşiktaş — modern Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views; ~500–700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Sunday is a good day to visit. Book tickets online as entry is by timed tour. Photography restrictions apply inside.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum, recently reopened in a stunning new building in Karaköy designed by Renzo Piano. Excellent collection of Turkish modern and contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Karaköy and Tophane neighborhoods — full of art galleries, design studios, and the famous Tophane narghile (hookah) cafés. Visit the Kılıç Ali Paşa Mosque (another Sinan masterpiece). Walk along the Bosphorus waterfront toward Beşiktaş.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to Cihangir neighborhood — a beloved bohemian hillside district with antique shops, art studios, and the best sunset views over the Bosphorus. Enjoy dinner in this local favorite area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or try a Karaköy-style breakfast at Karaköy Lokantası
meals.lunch: Karaköy Lokantası — stylish lokanta with updated Turkish classics; ~350–450 TRY per person
meals.dinner: Cihangir neighborhood restaurant — try Zübeyir Ocakbaşı for charcoal-grilled meats in a local atmosphere; ~350–500 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern is closed on Mondays — check opening days before visiting and adjust the schedule if needed. The Tophane narghile cafés are a unique cultural experience worth trying in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş (1–1.5 hours) to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands in the Sea of Marmara. No motor vehicles allowed — explore by horse-drawn carriage or bicycle. Visit the historic Aya Yorgi Monastery on the hilltop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle and explore Büyükada's charming Victorian-era wooden mansions, pine forests, and quiet beaches. Swim at one of the small beaches if weather permits (May can be warm enough). Enjoy the peaceful pace — a world away from Istanbul's bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon (allow time — ferries fill up on weekends). Arrive back at Kabataş by 19:00–20:00. Quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before ferry departure
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a Büyükada restaurant overlooking the sea — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and meze; ~350–450 TRY per person
meals.dinner: Simple and relaxed dinner near Sultanahmet — try a neighborhood pide restaurant; ~200–250 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Check the İDO ferry schedule in advance — ferries run frequently in summer. Bicycle rental on Büyükada costs approximately 100–150 TRY per hour. Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the magnificent 6th-century underground Byzantine cistern beneath Sultanahmet, with 336 marble columns and the famous Medusa head bases. Recently renovated with atmospheric lighting. Then visit the nearby Binbirdirek Cistern (less crowded, equally impressive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Küçük Ayasofya Camii (Little Hagia Sophia) — a stunning 6th-century Byzantine church converted to a mosque, often overlooked by tourists. Walk through the quieter southern Sultanahmet streets toward the Sea of Marmara waterfront. Visit the Sokollu Mehmet Paşa Mosque.
day_by_day.evening: Final grand evening in Istanbul — take a sunset walk along the old city walls near Yedikule or along the Marmara coast. Enjoy a special farewell dinner at one of Sultanahmet's best rooftop restaurants with views of the illuminated skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a neighborhood börekçi (pastry shop) — try various börek types (cheese, spinach, meat) with ayran; ~100–150 TRY
meals.dinner: Panorama 1453 area or Deraliye Ottoman Restaurant — a celebratory final dinner with Ottoman imperial recipes; ~500–700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern is best visited when it opens (9:00) to enjoy the atmospheric lighting before crowds arrive. Book tickets online. This is a good day for last-minute souvenir shopping in the Grand Bazaar area.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — depending on departure time, take a last slow walk through Sultanahmet. Visit any missed sites or simply sit in a çay bahçesi (tea garden) in Gülhane Park with views of the Bosphorus. Pack and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Istanbul Airport (allow 60–90 min travel time depending on traffic). Browse the excellent duty-free shops at Istanbul Airport for last-minute Turkish delights, teas, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a classic Turkish breakfast at a neighborhood spot — savor it slowly
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before transfer — try a fresh gözleme (stuffed flatbread) from a street vendor; ~80–120 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transfer — Istanbul traffic can be unpredictable, especially in the afternoon. The airport metro (M11) is the most reliable option. Keep some Turkish Lira for tips and last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Istanbul Airport to your boutique hotel in Sultanahmet via chauffeured Mercedes-Benz S-Class or similar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Sultanahmet boutique hotel and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation stroll through the Sultanahmet square to absorb the atmosphere — admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia from the square, and visit the nearby Hippodrome (Sultanahmet Meydanı) to see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column. No entry queues, just a relaxed first impression of the historic peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on your hotel's terrace or a nearby rooftop bar with panoramic views of the Sea of Marmara and the illuminated Blue Mosque. Followed by a welcome dinner at a premium Ottoman-cuisine restaurant in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome mezze and Turkish tea at the hotel or a nearby upscale café such as Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi for a classic introduction to local flavors.
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant (inside the Ottoman Imperial Hotel) — refined Ottoman palace cuisine in a historic setting, with dishes inspired by 16th-century imperial recipes. Expect slow-roasted lamb, stuffed vine leaves with saffron rice, and baklava for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Request early check-in in advance. Confirm private transfer booking before departure. Hotel concierge should brief you on the 13-day program upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural achievements. A specialist art-history guide will walk you through its Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman additions, massive dome, and layered 1,500-year history. Book a private early-access slot to avoid crowds (arrange via hotel concierge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Topkapi Palace complex — the nerve center of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and the Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters with a private guide, and the stunning tiled Pavilion of the Holy Mantle. Stroll through the palace gardens overlooking the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grand Bazaar neighborhood on foot as evening light falls over the covered lanes. Then enjoy a premium dinner in Beyoğlu or Karaköy, a short taxi ride away.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the hotel — a spread of white cheese, olives, tomatoes, cucumbers, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), simit, and fresh tea.
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside the Topkapi Palace grounds — a historic institution serving traditional Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views. Try the lamb stew and lentil soup.
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant (Marmara Pera Hotel rooftop) — Chef Mehmet Gürs's celebrated New Anatolian cuisine with sweeping panoramic views of Istanbul. Tasting menu with wine pairing recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Harem requires a separate ticket — book in advance. Dress modestly for Hagia Sophia (shoulders and knees covered). Private guide for both sites can be arranged through the hotel for approximately 4–6 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the magnificent 6th-century underground Byzantine water reservoir with 336 marble columns, atmospheric lighting, and the famous Medusa head bases. Follow with a visit to the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex (three museums in one: Classical Antiquities, Ancient Orient, and Tiled Kiosk) — one of the world's great yet undervisited collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü with a private culinary guide who will introduce you to the best stalls for saffron, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and specialty teas. Then take a private Bosphorus cruise on a chartered wooden gulet or luxury motorboat, sailing past the Dolmabahçe Palace waterfront, the Ortaköy Mosque, and under the iconic Bosphorus Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for a relaxed evening. Attend the atmospheric Sound and Light show at the Blue Mosque (seasonal, check schedule) or simply enjoy a sunset walk along the sea walls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a special spread with börek (flaky pastry), menemen (Turkish eggs), and fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice.
meals.lunch: Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar — a legendary Istanbul institution since 1901, serving traditional Turkish dishes in a beautiful tiled dining room. Try the sea bass in parchment and the cold yogurt soup.
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant — internationally acclaimed for its meticulous recreation of Ottoman imperial banquet recipes sourced from 15th and 16th-century palace kitchen records. Reserve the garden terrace.

day_by_day.notes: The private Bosphorus cruise can be arranged for 2–3 hours in the afternoon (approx. 15:00–18:00) for the best light. Ensure the culinary guide for the Spice Bazaar is booked at least 48 hours in advance through a specialist food tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — experience the interior's 20,000 hand-painted Iznik tiles, six minarets, and soaring domed space with your guide explaining its history and architecture. Note: mosque closes to visitors during prayer times, so plan around the schedule. Follow with a visit to the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) nearby — housing spectacular late Roman/Byzantine floor mosaics discovered beneath the old imperial palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — Sinan's masterpiece atop the Third Hill, offering the finest panoramic views over the Golden Horn. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Wander the charming Süleymaniye neighborhood, a less-touristy area with antique shops and traditional craftsmen.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge to Karaköy and climb to the Galata Tower for sunset views over the entire city. Then explore the lively Karaköy neighborhood for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe — a beautifully restored 16th-century Ottoman soup kitchen (imaret) adjacent to the Süleymaniye Mosque, now serving traditional Ottoman cuisine in a historic courtyard. Try the lamb with dried fruits and the semolina halva.
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası — a beloved upscale meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Karaköy serving elevated versions of classic Turkish dishes and meze. Excellent rakı selection. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque is closed to tourists during the five daily prayers (approximately 30–90 minutes each). Check the prayer schedule and plan your visit for mid-morning. Modest dress required (headscarves provided at entrance for women).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — depart from Kabataş ferry terminal on a private or first-class ferry to Büyükada (the largest island). Explore by horse-drawn carriage or bicycle (no cars allowed) through pine-forested hills, Victorian-era mansions, and Greek Orthodox monasteries. Visit the hilltop Monastery of St. George with sweeping sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — visit the historic Splendid Palace Hotel (even if just for a drink), browse the charming waterfront promenade, and enjoy the relaxed island pace far from the city bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul. Arrive back in Sultanahmet by early evening for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before ferry departure (ferry typically departs around 09:00–09:30).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium seafood restaurant on Büyükada's waterfront — try the grilled sea bream, octopus salad, and fresh calamari with a glass of local white wine. Recommended: Milto Restaurant or Princess Restaurant on the island.
meals.dinner: Seven Hills Restaurant, Sultanahmet — rooftop terrace with extraordinary views of the Blue Mosque and Sea of Marmara, serving refined Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine. Perfect for a relaxed evening after the island day trip.

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (before 09:30) to maximize island time. Private ferry charter is available for a more exclusive experience. Comfortable walking shoes essential for the island. May weather in Istanbul is typically warm and pleasant — ideal for this excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private hammam (Turkish bath) experience — book an exclusive session at one of Istanbul's historic imperial hammams. The Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584 by Sinan) or the Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı (16th century, recently restored) offer premium private kese (exfoliation) and köpük (foam massage) treatments. A deeply cultural and restorative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — containing what many scholars consider the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, depicting the life of Christ and the Virgin Mary in stunning detail. Follow with a walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Land Walls (5th century AD), the longest surviving Byzantine fortification.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh. Evening at leisure or optional visit to a traditional Turkish music performance (fasıl or classical Ottoman music) at a meyhane in Beyoğlu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Asitane Restaurant (near Chora Church) — conveniently located and serving exceptional Ottoman cuisine. A second visit is worthwhile given the menu's depth and quality.
meals.dinner: Neolokal Restaurant (SALT Galata building, Karaköy) — Chef Maksut Aşkar's celebrated modern Anatolian cuisine using heirloom ingredients and traditional techniques reimagined. One of Istanbul's most critically acclaimed fine-dining destinations. Full tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam well in advance — private slots at Hürrem Sultan Hamamı fill quickly. The Chora Church may have limited access depending on ongoing restoration work; confirm status before visiting. A private driver is recommended for the Edirnekapı area as it is further from Sultanahmet.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul — take a short Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to Kadıköy. Explore the vibrant Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a sprawling food market beloved by locals, with outstanding stalls selling cheeses, pickles, fresh produce, cured meats, and pastries. Join a private food walk with a local guide for tastings and cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll the charming Moda neighborhood of Kadıköy — tree-lined streets, independent bookshops, vintage stores, and café culture. Visit the Moda seaside promenade for views back toward the European skyline. Then explore Üsküdar — one of Istanbul's oldest and most atmospheric Asian-side neighborhoods — visiting the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque and the waterfront with its classic views of the Bosphorus and the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi).
day_by_day.evening: Return to European Istanbul by ferry at sunset — one of the most beautiful urban ferry rides in the world. Dinner in Beyoğlu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — legendary chef Musa Dağdeviren's restaurant celebrating the diverse regional cuisines of Anatolia. Rotating daily menu of rare dishes from across Turkey. A culinary pilgrimage that food lovers worldwide make specifically for this experience.
meals.dinner: Nusr-Et Steakhouse (Etiler or Nişantaşı branch) or alternatively Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus — both offer premium meat-focused menus with exceptional wine lists and city or Bosphorus views.

day_by_day.notes: The Kadıköy food walk guide should be booked in advance through a reputable culinary tour company. Friday is a busy day at mosques — plan Üsküdar visit to avoid Friday noon prayer congestion. The Maiden's Tower can be visited by short boat transfer and has a restaurant inside.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace that replaced Topkapi as the administrative center of the empire. Marvel at the 285-room complex, the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (a gift from Queen Victoria), the ceremonial halls, and the ornate Harem section. Guided visits are mandatory and private tours can be arranged.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Beşiktaş neighborhood and visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) — housing magnificent imperial caïques (royal rowing boats), historic maps, and Ottoman maritime artifacts. Then stroll through the upscale Nişantaşı district — Istanbul's answer to the Champs-Élysées, with flagship luxury boutiques, designer stores, and elegant cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a world-class cocktail experience at one of Istanbul's premier rooftop bars — 5. Kat in Beyoğlu or Leb-i Derya Richmond — before a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Tuğra Restaurant at the Çırağan Palace Kempinski — dine in the restored banquet hall of a 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus waterfront. The setting alone is extraordinary. Classic Ottoman and Turkish cuisine at the highest level.
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant (Tomtom Suites, Beyoğlu) — intimate fine dining with French-influenced modern Turkish cuisine, exceptional wine cellar, and beautiful city views. One of Istanbul's most refined dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires advance booking for private tours. Photography is restricted in parts of the palace. The Çırağan Palace Kempinski lunch reservation should be made several days in advance — request a Bosphorus-view table.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern (İstanbul Modern Sanat Müzesi) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum, recently relocated to a stunning new Renzo Piano-designed building on the Bosphorus in Karaköy. Explore the permanent collection of modern Turkish art and any special exhibitions. The architecture and Bosphorus views are themselves worth the visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Pera neighborhood (Beyoğlu) — visit the Pera Museum housing the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting by Osman Hamdi Bey and important Orientalist art collections. Stroll the historic İstiklal Avenue (Istiklal Caddesi) — a 1.4km pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European-style buildings, embassies, bookshops, music stores, and hidden courtyards (pasajlar). Discover the ornate Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and the Balık Pazarı (Fish Market).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — a deeply moving Sufi spiritual ritual. The Hodjapasha Cultural Center near Sirkeci offers high-quality performances in a beautifully restored 15th-century bathhouse. Book tickets in advance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Galata House Restaurant — a converted 19th-century British jail turned intimate restaurant in the Galata neighborhood, serving Georgian-influenced Turkish cuisine. Unique and atmospheric.
meals.dinner: Hünkar Restaurant (Nişantaşı or Fatih branch) — a historic Istanbul institution since 1950 serving classic Turkish home cooking elevated to a fine level. Famous for its hünkar beğendi (sultan's delight — lamb on smoked eggplant purée) and slow-cooked stews.

day_by_day.notes: The Whirling Dervishes ceremony lasts approximately 1.5 hours. Photography with flash is not permitted during the ceremony. Book Hodjapasha tickets at least 2–3 days in advance. Sunday can be busy on İstiklal Avenue — visit in the early afternoon before the evening crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Edirne (approximately 2.5 hours by private car) — the former Ottoman capital before Constantinople. Visit the magnificent Selimiye Mosque, considered by its architect Sinan to be his greatest achievement (surpassing even the Süleymaniye). A UNESCO World Heritage Site of breathtaking proportions and beauty. Also visit the Eski Cami (Old Mosque) with its monumental calligraphy and the Üç Şerefeli Mosque.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Edirne's historic bazaar district — visit the Bedesten and the Ali Paşa Covered Bazaar. Browse shops selling Edirne's famous products: liver (ciğer) dishes, cheese, and the distinctive purple-striped Edirne soap. Visit the Edirne Palace ruins (Saray-ı Cedid-i Amire) — once the largest palace in the Ottoman Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car, arriving in the early evening. Relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Edirne — try the city's legendary tava ciğeri (fried liver) at a traditional lokanta near the bazaar, a dish Edirne is famous for throughout Turkey. Follow with Edirne's famous dondurma (ice cream) for dessert.
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin, Sultanahmet — one of Istanbul's finest and most authentic fish restaurants, housed in a charming Ottoman-era building. Seasonal fresh fish, outstanding meze, and excellent rakı. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 07:30–08:00 to maximize time in Edirne. A private car with a knowledgeable driver-guide is strongly recommended. Edirne is approximately 235km from Istanbul — the journey is straightforward via the TEM motorway. This is a full and rewarding day; pace accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private cooking class with a master Turkish chef — held in a traditional Istanbul kitchen or a dedicated culinary school. Learn to prepare a full Ottoman-Turkish menu: from making börek and dolma from scratch, to preparing a classic lamb güveç (clay pot stew) and rolling out baklava dough. This is a hands-on, deeply immersive cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rüstem Paşa Mosque in Eminönü — a hidden gem by Sinan, famous for its extraordinary density of Iznik tiles covering virtually every surface in dazzling blue, turquoise, and red floral patterns. Smaller and more intimate than the great imperial mosques, it is arguably the most beautiful tiled interior in Istanbul. Then explore the surrounding Tahtakale and Eminönü waterfront — a sensory explosion of street vendors, ferries, and historic warehouses.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening stroll through the illuminated Sultanahmet — the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia lit up at night are among the most beautiful sights in the world. Farewell cocktails and a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the morning cooking class — most culinary programs include a sit-down lunch of the food cooked.
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant at the Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet — elegant fine dining in the restored 19th-century Ottoman prison, with a menu of refined Mediterranean and Turkish cuisine. Impeccable service and setting for a memorable evening.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be booked at least one week in advance — recommended providers include Istanbul Culinary Institute or private chef experiences arranged through the hotel. The Rüstem Paşa Mosque is elevated above the street — look for the entrance staircase beneath the market arcade.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) in Sultanahmet — housed in the 16th-century palace of Ibrahim Pasha, the collection spans 1,400 years of Islamic art including extraordinary Seljuk and Ottoman carpets, calligraphy, ceramics, and manuscripts. One of the world's great Islamic art collections, yet surprisingly uncrowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Balat and Fener neighborhoods along the Golden Horn — two of Istanbul's oldest and most atmospheric districts, home to the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, historic synagogues, Armenian churches, and crumbling Ottoman mansions. These neighborhoods have become a hub for boutique galleries, artisan workshops, and specialty coffee shops while retaining their historic character. A private walking tour with a local historian is ideal.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the Pierre Loti Hill (Eyüp) — take the cable car up to the hilltop café that the French novelist Pierre Loti frequented in the 19th century, overlooking the Golden Horn and the city's minarets. Then visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque — one of the holiest sites in Istanbul, with a beautiful courtyard and the ornate tomb of Eyüp el-Ensari.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Fener Rum Patrikhanesi area — lunch at one of the charming local restaurants in Balat. Try Forno Balat for artisan bread and light dishes, or a traditional meyhane in the neighborhood for fresh meze and grilled fish.
meals.dinner: Vogue Restaurant (Beşiktaş) — a long-standing Istanbul classic with panoramic Bosphorus views, serving contemporary international cuisine with strong Turkish influences. Excellent sushi and seafood alongside Turkish specialties. A stylish and celebratory setting.

day_by_day.notes: The Balat/Fener walking tour is best done in the afternoon when the light is golden and the neighborhoods are most atmospheric. Wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobbled and hilly. The Pierre Loti cable car (teleferik) runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure in Sultanahmet — a last Turkish breakfast at the hotel, followed by a relaxed return to any favorite spots or last-minute shopping. Visit the Grand Bazaar one final time for any remaining souvenir purchases — look for hand-painted ceramics, quality Turkish carpets, gold jewelry, pashmina scarves, or premium Turkish delight and coffee to take home. The hotel concierge can recommend trusted vendors for authentic, quality goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport (IST) for departure. Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure. Istanbul Airport has excellent premium lounges — the Turkish Airlines CIP Lounge (iGA Lounge) is one of the finest airport lounges in the world, with a full restaurant, spa, cinema, and golf simulator.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast at the hotel — savor every element of the spread: the fresh simit, the kaymak with honey, the strong black tea in tulip glasses.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a café near the Grand Bazaar — try Havuzlu Restaurant inside the bazaar itself (one of Istanbul's oldest restaurant interiors) for a final bowl of lentil soup and grilled köfte.
meals.dinner: Dining at the airport lounge or on board — the Turkish Airlines Business Class meal service is exceptional if flying TK.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the hotel (typically until 14:00–15:00 for premium guests) to allow a relaxed final morning. Confirm private transfer booking the evening before. Ensure all purchased items (ceramics, carpets, etc.) are properly packed and declared if necessary. Keep receipts for VAT refund claims at the airport — Turkey offers tax refunds for non-EU visitors on purchases above a certain threshold.

query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026
